dedupe_keys.name: circular business model experimentation agent based model of a local biodigestion network turning organic waste into biogas and digestate

description: This agent-based model explores how the design of a circular business model affects whether a local biodigestion network survives. It was published in the CoMSES library by Kasper Lange, Gijsbert Korevaar, Igor Nikolic and Paulien Herder and passed peer review there (version 1.1.0, 2021). A processor takes organic waste from local suppliers and turns it into biogas and nutrient-rich digestate for local reuse. Value captured, measured as cash flow per tonne of waste per agent relative to the initial state, uses the cost of incineration as a benchmark, and interactions with the waste incinerator and actor behaviour moderate the outcome; actors may leave the network when it no longer pays. The code is free to download from CoMSES under a CC-BY-4.0 licence, with a DOI. Caveats: the network is stylised, and results depend on the cost assumptions. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: testing whether local organic waste treatment is viable against incineration, in waste system planning. Related records: the EPA WARM model (model-epa-warm-waste-reduction-model) estimates the emissions side of such choices.
inputs: Organic waste suppliers and a biodigestion processor
Business model design, incineration costs as benchmark, actor behaviour
name: Circular business model experimentation: agent-based model of a local biodigestion network turning organic waste into biogas and digestate
outputs: Value captured (cash flow per tonne of waste per agent) and network survival over time
provider: Igor Nikolic, Kasper Pieter Hendrik Lange, Gijsbert Korevaar, Paulien Herder (CoMSES Computational Model Library)
